reasons: Party mapping is correct: Corio is the licensee/customer and Commerce One the licensor/vendor, and the redline moves rights in our favour (affiliate and successor assignment for Corio without consent; consent-plus-reasonableness and a competitor bar only on Commerce One), matching the ASSIGN preferred position.

The removal of the competitor carve-back as applied to our M&A/asset-sale assignment directly cures the identified deviation (vendor leverage over our corporate transactions) and the clause retains the successors/permitted assigns and null-and-void sentences, so the rewrite is scoped to what the rule requires.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.783 changed-character ratio) is justified here: converting a symmetric consent bar into an asymmetric one cannot be done with a small insertion, and no unrelated terms were disturbed.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook rationale, and offers the mutual notice-based fallback; the rationale's statement that Section 11 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right is consistent with the cited text, so no further deletion is needed.

Minor (non-blocking) note: the redline leaves Corio's non-affiliate/non-successor assignments unrestricted rather than subject to consent not unreasonably withheld; this is more favourable than strictly necessary but remains within the preferred position and is easy to trade back if challenged.
